questions.stem: In triangle ABC, AB = 9 cm, BC = 12 cm, and angle ABC = 110 degrees. Find the length AC to 1 decimal place.
A field is shaped as a triangle with sides 85 m, 110 m, and 130 m. Find the area of the field to the nearest m squared. (Hint: first find an angle using the Cosine Rule.)

Town A is due north of town C. Town B is on a bearing of 065 degrees from A and on a bearing of 320 degrees from C. AB = 15 km. The angle ABC = 75 degrees. Find BC to 1 decimal place using the Sine Rule.
questions.explanation: Angle A = 65 degrees (bearing from north). Angle C = 360 - 320 = 40 degrees. Angle B = 180 - 65 - 40 = 75 degrees. By Sine Rule: BC/sin(A) = AB/sin(C). BC = 15 x sin(65)/sin(40) = 15 x 0.9063/0.6428 = 21.2 km (1 d.p.).

A quadrilateral ABCD has AB = 5 cm, BC = 7 cm, angle ABC = 90 degrees, CD = 8 cm, and angle BCD = 115 degrees. To find AD, which diagonal should you draw first to split the problem into two triangles?
questions.explanation: Drawing AC creates triangle ABC (right-angled at B, so AC = sqrt(25+49) = sqrt(74)) and triangle ACD. In triangle ACD, you can find angle ACD = angle BCD - angle BCA, then use the Cosine Rule with AC, CD, and the included angle to find AD.
